record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.original_question: Which improved branching-ratio measurements of T = 1 superallowed beta decays, especially the superallowed branch of carbon-10, are needed to reduce the limiting experimental uncertainty in superallowed-decay Vud extractions and scalar-current limits?

evidence.quote: Generally, branching ratio measurements of T = 1 superallowed decays are the limiting factor and are a significant priority for the community.
branching ratio uncertainty in the superallowed branch of 10C. A recent determination was performed at ISOLDE (55), with a number of experiments still in the planning stage.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the extraction of the up-quark CKM matrix element V_ud and in the derivation of limits on hypothetical scalar currents from nuclear β decay, one uses an ensemble of T = 1, 0+ → 0+ "superallowed" Fermi β decays. For each such transition the corrected ft-value (Ft) requires precise knowledge of (i) the transition Q-value, (ii) the parent half-life, and (iii) the branching ratio of the superallowed branch. At present the dominant experimental uncertainty in many cases comes from the branching ratio.

Identify which T = 1 superallowed 0+ → 0+ β-decay branching-ratio measurements would, if improved, yield the largest reduction in the experimental uncertainty of:
(a) the V_ud value extracted from the ensemble of superallowed Ft-values, and
(b) the limit on a possible Fierz interference term b_F (and hence on a beyond-Standard-Model scalar charged current) inferred from the same ensemble.

In particular, quantify the precision now needed in the branching ratio of the superallowed branch of 10C(0+, g.s.) → 10B(0+, 1.74 MeV) + e+ + ν_e, given the most recent experimental determination of this branching ratio (1.4638(50)%), and specify which other transitions among the canonical superallowed set (e.g. 14O, 22Mg, 26mAl, 34Cl, 38mK, 42Sc, 46V, 50Mn, 54Co, 62Ga, 74Rb) require improved branching-ratio measurements to advance both the V_ud determination and the scalar-current sensitivity.
artifact.category_tag: Superallowed beta decay and Vud extraction
artifact.status_search_result: The question is an open experimental program. A recent precise determination of the 10C superallowed branching ratio (1.4638(50)%) was performed at ISOLDE (CERN) and published in 2020, and additional measurements of 10C and other T = 1 superallowed branches remain in planning or in progress. No measurement campaign has yet reduced the branching-ratio uncertainty to a level where it is no longer the limiting experimental input for V_ud and scalar-current limits.

status_evidence.title: Branching ratio of the super-allowed beta decay of 10C
status_evidence.snippet: Final result for the super-allowed decay branch of 10C measured at ISOLDE: 1.4638(50)%.
status_evidence.claim: A recent precise 10C branching ratio measurement exists, but further improvements are still being pursued.

status_evidence.title: Precise branching-ratio measurement for the superallowed decay (Phys. Rev. C 101, 045501)
status_evidence.snippet: Precision branching-ratio measurements for superallowed 0+→0+ emitters continue to be reported as needed inputs to the V_ud determination.
status_evidence.claim: Branching ratios for superallowed decays remain an active experimental priority.
